text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria police post reward of four million naira for any information leading to arrest of perpetrators of two bomb blasts in Lagos this week.
- Federal high court sets December 27 for ruling on whether state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp can insure its assets with other firms and ditch state insurer NICON.

- Octogenerian leader of opposition NADECO group, Michael Ajasin, who was admitted in hospital this week for an undisclosed ailment, is getting better and is expected back home this weekend, his wife said.

- Nigeria Airways ordered by government to close its New York office and to hand it over to Nigerian consulate in the U.S. city; U.S. banned flights from Nigeria since 1993 citing insecurity at Nigerian airports.
- Exiled Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka denies involvement in spate of bombings that have rocked Lagos in past few days.
- Editor of independent weekly magazine The Week, Godwin Agbroko, has been arrested by security men, his magazine said.
